arxiv-2101-00224.title: New phenomena in laser-assisted leptonic decays of the negatively charged boson W − W^{-}
arxiv-2101-00224.creator: S Mouslih, M Jakha, I Dahiri, S Taj, B Manaut, E. Siher
arxiv-2101-00224.description: Abstract The majority of studies and experiments performed at electron-positron colliders over the last two decades have focused on studying W W and Z Z weak force-carrying bosons and accurately measuring all their properties, not only because they play an important role in establishing Standard Model theory and providing an accurate test of its predictions of particle interactions, but also

arxiv-2103-15017.title: H-GAN: the power of GANs in your Hands
arxiv-2103-15017.creator: Sergiu Oprea 1 , Giorgos Karvounas 2 , Pablo Martinez-Gonzalez 1 , Nikolaos Kyriazis 2 , Sergio Orts-Escolano 3 , Iason Oikonomidis 2 , Alberto Garcia-Garcia 4 , Aggeliki Tsoli 2 , Jose Garcia-Rodriguez 1 , and Antonis Argyros 2
arxiv-2103-15017.description: Abstract We present HandGAN (H-GAN) , a cycle-consistent adversarial learning approach implementing multi-scale perceptual discriminators. It is designed to translate synthetic images of hands to the real domain. Synthetic hands provide complete ground-truth annotations, yet they are not representative of the target distribution of real-world data.

arxiv-2207-08324.title: Formal balls of 𝖰 {\sf Q} -categories
arxiv-2207-08324.creator: Xianbo Yang, Dexue Zhang
arxiv-2207-08324.description: Abstract The construction of the formal ball model for metric spaces due to Edalat and Heckmann was generalized to Q -categories by Kostanek and Waszkiewicz. This paper concerns the influence of the structure of the quantale Q on the connection between Yoneda completeness of 𝖰 {\sf Q} -categories and directed completeness of their sets of formal balls.

arxiv-2305-08572.title: Estimating the Causal Effects of Natural Logic Features in Neural NLI Models
arxiv-2305-08572.creator: Julia Rozanova, Marco Valentino, André Freitas, University of Manchester, United Kingdom, {firstname.lastname}@manchester.ac.uk, Idiap Research Institute, Switzerland, {firstname.lastname}@idiap.ch
arxiv-2305-08572.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Julia Rozanova, Marco Valentino, André Freitas, University of Manchester, United Kingdom, {firstname.lastname}@manchester.ac.uk, Idiap Research Institute, Switzerland, {firstname.lastname}@idiap.ch. Rigorous evaluation of the causal effects of semantic features on language model predictions can be hard to achieve for natural language reasoning problems.

arxiv-2506-11430.title: Auto-Connect: Connectivity-Preserving RigFormer with Direct Preference Optimization
arxiv-2506-11430.creator: Jingfeng Guo, Jian Liu, Jinnan Chen, Shiwei Mao, Changrong Hu, Puhua Jiang, [5pt] Junlin Yu, Jing Xu, Qi Liu , Lixin Xu, Zhuo Chen, Chunchao Guo, [5pt] South China University of Technology, [5pt] Hong Kong University of Science, Technology National University of Singapore, [5pt] Tsinghua Shenzhen In
arxiv-2506-11430.description: Abstract We introduce Auto-Connect, a novel approach for automatic rigging that explicitly preserves skeletal connectivity through a connectivity-preserving tokenization scheme. Unlike previous methods that predict bone positions represented as two joints or first predict points before determining connectivity, our method employs special tokens to define endpoints for each joint’s children and for each hierarchical layer, effectively automating connectivity relationships.

arxiv-2510-05485.title: TensorBLEU: Vectorized GPU-based BLEU Score Implementation for Per-Sentence In-Training Evaluation
arxiv-2510-05485.creator: Adam Filipek (adamfilipek@rxai.dev)
arxiv-2510-05485.description: Abstract Modern natural language processing models have achieved unprecedented scale, yet the tools for their evaluation often remain a computational bottleneck, limiting the pace of research. This is particularly acute for in-training evaluation metrics, such as per-sentence reward signals in Reinforcement Learning, which must operate efficiently on batches of token IDs directly on the GPU.

camilla-picture-of-youth.title: Camilla Picture of Youth
camilla-picture-of-youth.creator: Burney, Fanny
camilla-picture-of-youth.description: First published in 1796, Camilla deals with the matrimonial concerns of a group of young people - Camilla Tyrold and her sisters, the daughters of a country parson, and their cousin Indiana Lynmere-and, in particular, with the love affair between Camilla herself and her eligible suitor, Edgar Mandlebert. The path of true love, however, is strewn with intrigue, contretemps and misunderstanding. ...

catholic-encyclopedia-1913-christmas.description: Article 'Christmas' from the Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), the 15-volume English-language reference work published 1907-1914 by Robert Appleton Company.

pmc-10599405.title: A Case of Disappearing Ascites: Late Presentation of Acute Portal Vein Thrombosis After a Motor Vehicle Accident
pmc-10599405.creator: Teresa Del Rio, Dayana Reveron, Susan Ramdhaney
pmc-10599405.description: Portal vein thrombosis (PVT) has been usually diagnosed as a complication secondary to cardiac, hepatic, and malignant etiologies, but it has rarely been described in the setting of blunt abdominal trauma. This case depicts an older male who presented to the emergency department with progressive ascites and lower extremity edema within two weeks after a motor vehicle accident (MVA).

pmc-10649706.title: Genetic Mapping for QTL Associated with Seed Nickel and Molybdenum Accumulation in the Soybean ‘Forrest’ by ‘Williams 82’ RIL Population
pmc-10649706.creator: Nacer Bellaloui, Dounya Knizia, Jiazheng Yuan, Qijian Song, Frances Betts, Teresa Register, Earl Williams, Naoufal Lakhssassi, Hamid Mazouz, Henry T. Nguyen, Khalid Meksem, Alemu Mengistu, My Abdelmajid Kassem
pmc-10649706.description: Understanding the genetic basis of seed Ni and Mo is essential. Since soybean is a major crop in the world and a major source for nutrients, including Ni and Mo, the objective of the current research was to map genetic regions (quantitative trait loci, QTL) linked to Ni and Mo concentrations in soybean seed.

pmc-10674603.title: West Nile Virus, an Underdiagnosed Cause of Acute Fever of Unknown Origin and Neurological Disease among Hospitalized Patients in South Africa
pmc-10674603.creator: Caitlin MacIntyre, Carla Lourens, Adriano Mendes, Maryke de Villiers, Theunis Avenant, Nicolette M. du Plessis, Fabian H. Leendertz, Marietjie Venter
pmc-10674603.description: West Nile virus (WNV), a mosquito-borne flavivirus, is endemic to South Africa. However, its contribution to acute febrile and neurological disease in hospitalized patients in South Africa is unknown. This study examined two patient cohorts for WNV using molecular testing and IgM serology with confirmation of serological results by viral neutralization tests (VNT) to address this knowledge gap.

pmc-10710703.title: The effect of parental diabetes prevention program participation on weight loss in dependent children: a prospective cohort study
pmc-10710703.creator: Namratha Atluri, Joshua Thariath, Laura N. McEwen, Wen Ye, MinKyoung Song, William H. Herman
pmc-10710703.description: IntroductionObesity has reached epidemic proportions in children and adolescents in the United States. Children’s behaviors are strongly influenced by parental behaviors, and weight loss in parents is positively associated with weight changes in their overweight/obese children. Research is limited on how parents’ National Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP) participation affects the health outcomes of their dependent children.

pmc-10750853.title: Recreational beneficiaries and their landscape dependencies across national estuary program sites: Tillamook Bay (OR) and Tampa Bay (FL), USA
pmc-10750853.creator: Chanda Jones Littles, Nathaniel S. Lewis, Theodore H. DeWitt, Matthew C. Harwell
pmc-10750853.description: This study aims to characterize the value associated with nature-based recreational opportunities and identify estuarine attributes most valued by users. With the National Ecosystem Service Classification System as a framework, we assessed the relationship between recreational beneficiary subclasses and ecological end-products available to beneficiaries in Tillamook Bay, OR, and Tampa Bay, FL estuaries.

pmc-11356177.title: Comparative Life Cycle Assessment of Bacterial and Thermochemical Retting of Hemp
pmc-11356177.creator: Yu Fu, Hongmei Gu, H Felix Wu, Sheldon Q Shi, Francisco Agrela
pmc-11356177.description: The processes of hemp bast fiber retting, forming, and drying offer the opportunity for value-added products such as natural fiber-reinforced composites. A new process for the retting of raw bast fibers through enzyme-triggered self-cultured bacterial retting was developed in the lab-scale setup.

pmc-11430833.title: Comparative Clinical Study of Surgical Performance of Quatera 700 versus Centurion and Signature Pro Phacoemulsification Systems
pmc-11430833.creator: Sri Ganesh, Sheetal Brar, Supriya Sriganesh, Hemali D Bhavsar
pmc-11430833.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PurposeTo compare the intra-operative surgical performance of Quatera 700 with Centurion and Signature Pro phacoemulsification systems.SettingNethradhama Superspeciality Eye Hospital, Bangalore, India.Study DesignProspective, interventional, 3-arm, randomized comparison study.MethodsA total of 180 non-consecutive eyes satisfying the eligibility criteria were recruited. N = 60 eyes were operated using each of the above systems, of which n = 30 eyes had LOCS III grade 1–2, and n = 30 eyes had grade 3–4 nuclear density.

pmc-11698194.title: A longitudinal study of healthcare workers’ mental health during Western Australia's unique policy response to COVID-19
pmc-11698194.creator: Elizabeth A. Newnham, Enrique L. P. Mergelsberg, Susanne Stanley, Sean Hood, Jessica Tearne, Antonio Celenza, Teresa Stevenson, Nahal Mavaddat, Gavin Demore, Hyranthi Kavanagh, Peter M. McEvoy
pmc-11698194.description: BackgroundWestern Australia's response to the COVID-19 pandemic was swift and effective in implementing public health protections and preventing the spread of the virus for the first 2 years. However, healthcare staff continued to be at increased risk of mental health concerns.

pmc-12592187.title: HBHA-ECSIT interaction disrupts macrophage autophagy to promote Mycobacterium tuberculosis persistence
pmc-12592187.creator: Yongqiang Li, Xiuping Jia, Xiaoying Wang, Huilian Qiao, Yueyun Ma
pmc-12592187.description: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains one of the most significant global health challenges exacerbated by latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI). Heparin-binding hemagglutinin (HBHA), a virulence factor of Mtb, plays a critical role in LTBI by inhibiting autophagy in macrophages, though the underlying molecular mechanism has remained unclear.

pmc-12690669.title: PDNO-06 PEDIATRIC POSTERIOR FOSSA RESECTIONS; A CASE SERIES OF CASES DONE IN A TERTIARY HOSPITAL
pmc-12690669.creator: Jalilarah Nassozi
pmc-12690669.description: BackgroundPediatric posterior fossa tumors are among the most common brain tumors in children. Surgical resection remains the cornerstone of treatment, to achieve maximal safe resection while minimizing neurological deficits. This case series presents our experience with pediatric posterior fossa tumor resections, highlighting the outcomes, complications, and factors influencing surgical success.
